data.narrative:
Heliux is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Alex Craig and Victor Jakubiuk that has raised $4.7M to date. The valuation landscape for early-stage robotics comprises one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Stage-progression analysis represents the primary applicable method. Using total raised ($4.7M, rounded to $5M as proxy for pre-valuation capital deployed) and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression from Seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. This method is appropriate given Heliux's capital profile and trajectory within the robotics sector.

Peer-median comparison was not applicable. While ten same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, the narrow filters—same-stage peers, adjacent-stage comparables, or similar valuation-tier companies—yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three required). A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $10M (low) to $14M (high), with a median of $12M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the strength of technical differentiation relative to existing portfolio players, go-to-market traction post-seed, and capital efficiency metrics relative to peer benchmarks. Additional fundraising signals or operational milestones would sharpen directional confidence.
